title: v1-chat: mitigate param-echo and stabilize fncall streaming frame recovery
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fix streaming duplication where system/instruction content could be echoed in final completions; improved fncall streaming frame reassembly and heartbeat recovery to reduce client-visible truncation and malformed structured outputs.
description:
Summary: This PR addresses two related classes of v1/chat compatibility issues surfaced in production and by customers: (1) 'param-echo' where the streaming path could emit fragments that duplicated system/instruction text into the final assembled completion, and (2) fragile fncall/structured-output streaming frames that could leave the client with partial JSON or missing function-call metadata after transient network disconnects.
Motivation: Customers migrating to the v1/chat compatibility layer observed occasional duplicated instructions in the final completion and incorrect fncall objects after reconnects; both reduce reliability for production apps (especially tool-calling and structured-output use cases). This change reduces duplication and makes streaming frame reassembly deterministic on reconnect and partial replays.
What changed (high level):
- Introduced a streaming "echo filter" at the param-negotiation boundary that identifies tokens/segments highly-correlated with pinned system/instruction parameters and suppresses them from the final merge unless there is model-confirmed divergence. The filter uses a lightweight prefix-match heuristic and confidence threshold derived from the runtime token scorer to avoid false positives.
- Reworked fncall streaming framing: fragments now include a 2-byte frame header (version + frag-index) and an end-sentinel marker. A heartbeat/ack sequence allows servers to mark frames as committed; clients reconnecting in the middle of a stream can request the last-committed index.
- Added final-payload reconciler that aggregates streaming logprobs and stop hints with the non-streamed completion generation step. This prevents the streaming path from overwriting canonical stop/logprob state.
- Tests and observability: added deterministic unit tests for param-echo heuristic, integration tests that simulate reconnect/failure during fncall streaming, and new metrics: streaming.frame_reassembly_failures, streaming.echo_suppressed_count.
Commits (summary):
- 1a3f2e9: add param-echo filter and unit tests
- 2b9e4c1: implement fncall frame header + sentinel, add frame commit/ack handshake
- 7c5d113: reconcile streaming logprob aggregation with final payload
- 9ae5b2f: integration tests for reconnect / partial frame replay
- c4d8f07: docs: console notes on heartbeat/compat
- f5b1a22: fix linting and race in frame ack path
Changed files (illustrative):
- server/streaming/echo_filter.go (new) — implements prefix similarity heuristic and integration with token scorer
- server/streaming/frame_protocol.go (modified) — adds headers, frag-index, and ack handling
- server/streaming/handler_test.go (modified/added) — tests for reconnect scenarios and fncall reassembly
- sdk/python/redwood/v1/chat_stream.py (modified) — client-side support for reconnect and committed-index request
- sdk/typescript/stream-client.ts (modified) — small compat helpers for browsers
- docs/compat/v1-chat-streaming.md (modified) — added section about heartbeat and canary rollout notes
Small snippet (illustrative) included in server/streaming/frame_protocol.go: "// frame header: version(1) | fragIndex(1) - allows deterministic reassembly across reconnects"
Tests:
- Unit: echo_filter_test.go covers prefix-collision cases, threshold tuning and false positive regression.
- Integration: simulated 3 reconnect scenarios with random drops; fncall object reassembled successfully in 98/100 runs locally; CI runs are deterministic via mocked runtime.
CI:
- Pre-merge pipeline: lint, unit, integration, e2e-candidate.
- Current run: all checks passed (lint warnings auto-fixed), integration harness passed 28/28 scenarios.
- Flaky tests noticed initially (integration: reconnect-flaky) were stabilized by increasing frame timeout from 100ms->250ms.
Review thread (highlights):
- Owen Patel (reviewer): "Please ensure we don't silently drop legitimate repeated text when model actually re-states an instruction intentionally (e.g., role-reflection). The heuristic needs an escape hatch." Maya: "Added an escape: if final-generation logprob mass on the prefix exceeds 0.6 we bypass suppression and mark as explicit-repeat in telemetry."
- Priya Singh: "Add e2e that runs a small tool-calling example through the python and TS clients to validate fncall JSON shape end-to-end." Maya: "Added python/ts e2e callers and wired them into the integration job; added OP-level assertion on fncall.name and args."
- Luis Fernandez: "Risk: consumers of the streaming format may not be able to handle the 2-byte header. Need a compatibility flag." Maya: "Default frame version is backward compatible: legacy clients ignore the header and server emits a compat fallback for older agent-headers. Documented in compat notes."
- Owen (approve after fixes): "LGTM — tests look good, metrics added. Please watch canary closely."
Release notes (in PR body): "Fixes param-echo duplication in v1/chat streaming path and improves fncall frame recovery on reconnects; no API change for callers, minor client-side updates available in SDKs for better reconnect handling."
Deployment plan and canary:
- Canary rollout to 10% of hosted v1-chat traffic for 48 hours; streaming.frame_reassembly_failures and streaming.echo_suppressed_count monitored with alert thresholds.
- If any regression >0.5% error rate in fncall shape, automatic rollback will be triggered.
Backwards compatibility:
- Server emits header but will continue to stream compat frames when client advertises legacy agent via User-Agent/Handshake.
- SDK updates (python/ts) are optional but recommended for deterministic reconnect behavior.
Follow-ups:
- ENG-2071: telemetry dashboards for echo suppression across customers.
- ENG-2104: explore ML-based prefix de-duplication using scoring model (longer-term).
Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-03 after approvals from Priya and Owen. Canary started immediately; initial canary metrics show reduced duplication events (telemetry drop ~78% on sample customers).
Known limitations:
- Very adversarial prompts that intentionally echo instruction tokens may still appear in final output when model logprob supports it (we preserve these via escape hatch).
- There is a small increase in server-side CPU for the echo heuristic (~1.8% at 95th), measured and included in the release notes for capacity planning.
If you want to test locally:
- Run `make integration` under server/streaming with MOCK_RUNTIME=1
- Python example: examples/streaming_fncall.py (calls new client reconnect helper)
notes: Canary metrics to be reviewed by SRE and Product on 2026-02-05; docs updated to include migration guidance for older clients.
